measurement_plan.brand_impressions_note: Brand campaign search impression share stayed at 95% or more every baseline week, so its impressions track branded searches. Keep its bids and budget unchanged through the read window.
measurement_plan.readable_note: Break-even lift 17.5% is above the new-customer noise floor of 2.1%, so a flight that pays back will show.

rule.scale: new-customer lift above 2.1% and cost per incremental new customer at or under $110
rule.retest: new-customer lift above its floor at up to $165 per incremental new customer, or new-customer lift at or below its floor while Direct new-user or branded-search lift is above its own

handoffs: incrementality-test-designer, if installed, for a stricter holdout design
offline-media-lift-analyst, if installed, for the full readout with intervals and a placebo check

readout.cross_check: 891 QR sessions in the test states against 308 incremental new customers. A scan is a visit, not a buyer, and viewers who type the name or search for it never scan, so neither count stands in for the other; the lift against control is the result.

search_console_brand_clicks_context.note: national, context only; Search Console has no state

readout.verdict_reason: New-customer lift 11.8% is above its 2.1% floor, at $143.13 per incremental new customer against the $110 target (retest band up to $165).
next_flight_changes: R2 reached 52,400 homes against 83,333 planned, at 10.85 ads per home: its segment is smaller than the tool estimated. Lower R2's weekly cap from 4 to 3 and plan it on the delivered reach, and move the spend it can't use to R1, which delivered 101.4% of plan at 8.27 per home.

The plan already put homes reached by both routes above 8 (combined average 9.16), and no seller can see the other's delivery. Next time plan each route on a different audience segment where the tools allow it, or lower each route's frequency until the combined average lands on 8.
Keep Kansas and Oklahoma held out and the brand campaign unchanged through the retest.

unknowns: R3 and R4 were not funded, so their delivery was not read.
Reach from Google Ads counts people, which the plan treats as households; the combined reach is an estimate that assumes the routes overlap at random.
